readings.title: Elihu Condemns Self-Righteousness
readings.subtitle: God is Greater Than Man
readings.text: [Job 35:1] And Elihu answered and said, [2] “Have you reckoned this for right? You have said, ‘My righteousness is more than <dn>El</dn>’s’? [3] “For you say, ‘What does it profit You? What do I gain more than if I sinned?’ [4] “Let me reply to you, And to your friends with you. [5] “Look at the heavens and see, And look at the clouds – they are higher than you. [6] “If you have sinned, what have you accomplished against <dn>Him</dn>? Or your transgressions are multiplied, what do you do to <dn>Him</dn>? [7] “If you are righteous, what do you give <dn>Him</dn>? Or what does <dn>He</dn> receive from your hand? [8] “Your wickedness affects a man like you, And your righteousness a son of man. [9] “Because of the multitude of oppressions they cry out; They cry out for help because of the arm of the mighty. [10] “But no one says, ‘Where is <dn>Eloah</dn> my <dn>Maker</dn>, <dn>Who</dn> gives songs in the night, [11] ‘<dn>Who</dn> teaches us more than the beasts of the earth, And makes us wiser than the birds of the heavens?’ [12] “There they cry out, but <dn>He</dn> does not answer, Because of the pride of evil men. [13] “Only, <dn>El</dn> does not hear falsity, Nor does the <dn>Almighty</dn> look on it. [14] “Although you say you do not see <dn>Him</dn>, Judgment is before <dn>Him</dn>, and you wait for <dn>Him</dn>. [15] “And now, because <dn>He</dn> has not visited in <dn>His</dn> displeasure, Nor has <dn>He</dn> acknowledged folly, [16] “Job opens his mouth in vain, He multiplies words without knowledge.”

readings.title: Elihu Proclaims God's Justice
readings.subtitle: Discipline and Deliverance
readings.text: [Job 36:1] And Elihu added and said, [2] “Wait for me a little, and let me show you That there are yet words for <dn>Eloah</dn>. [3] “I bring my knowledge from afar, And ascribe righteousness to my <dn>Maker</dn>. [4] “For truly my words are not false; <dn>One</dn> perfect in knowledge is with you. [5] “See, <dn>El</dn> is mighty, but rejects no one; <dn>He</dn> is mighty in strength of heart. [6] “<dn>He</dn> does not preserve the life of the wrong, But <dn>He</dn> gives right-ruling to the poor. [7] “<dn>He</dn> does not withdraw <dn>His</dn> eyes from the righteous; But they are on the throne with kings, For <dn>He</dn> has seated them forever, and they are exalted. [8] “And if they are bound in shackles, Caught in cords of affliction, [9] “Then <dn>He</dn> declares to them their work and their transgressions, That they have acted proudly. [10] “And <dn>He</dn> opens their ear to discipline, And commands that they turn back from wickedness. [11] “If they obey and serve <dn>Him</dn>, They spend their days in goodness, And their years in pleasures. [12] “But if they do not obey, They perish by the sword, And they die without knowledge. [13] “But the defiled in heart heap up wrath; They do not cry for help when <dn>He</dn> binds them. [14] “Their being dies in youth, And their life is among the sodomites. [15] “<dn>He</dn> delivers the poor in their affliction, And opens their ears in oppression. [16] “And <dn>He</dn> would have also turned you out of distress, Into a broad place where there is no constraint; And what was set on your table would be filled with fatness. [17] “But you are filled with the judgment of the wrong; Judgment and right-ruling take hold. [18] “Because there is wrath, beware lest <dn>He</dn> entice you with scorn! And let not a great ransom turn you aside. [19] “Would <dn>He</dn> value your riches? No, not gold, nor all the forces of strength. [20] “Do not long for the night, For peoples to be cut off in their place. [21] “Take heed, do not turn to wickedness, For you have chosen this rather than affliction.

readings.title: The Majesty of God in Nature
readings.subtitle: Rain, Clouds, and Lightning
readings.text: [Job 36:22] “See, <dn>El</dn> acts exaltedly by <dn>His</dn> power. Who is a <dn>Teacher</dn> like <dn>Him</dn>? [23] “Who has appointed <dn>Him</dn> <dn>His</dn> way? Or who has said, ‘You have done unrighteousness’? [24] “Remember that you should praise <dn>His</dn> work, Which men have sung. [25] “All men have looked at it; Man looks from afar. [26] “See, <dn>El</dn> is great, and we do not know; The number of <dn>His</dn> years is unsearchable. [27] “For <dn>He</dn> draws up drops of water, Which distil as rain from the mist, [28] “Which the clouds drop, Pour upon man in abundance. [29] “Also, does one understand the spreading of clouds, The thundering of <dn>His</dn> booth? [30] “See, <dn>He</dn> has spread <dn>His</dn> light upon it, And covered the roots of the sea. [31] “For by them <dn>He</dn> judges the peoples; <dn>He</dn> gives food in abundance. [32] “<dn>He</dn> covers <dn>His</dn> hands with lightning, And commands it to strike. [33] “<dn>His</dn> thunder declares it, The cattle also, concerning that which is coming up.

readings.title: The Thunder of His Voice
readings.subtitle: Elihu Trembles at God's Power
readings.text: [Job 37:1] “At this also my heart trembles, And leaps from its place. [2] “Hear attentively the trembling of <dn>His</dn> voice, And the rumbling that comes from <dn>His</dn> mouth. [3] “<dn>He</dn> lets it loose under all the heavens, And <dn>His</dn> lightning to the ends of the earth. [4] “After it a voice roars; <dn>He</dn> thunders with the voice of <dn>His</dn> excellency; And <dn>He</dn> does not hold them back when <dn>His</dn> voice is heard. [5] “<dn>El</dn> thunders wondrously with <dn>His</dn> voice; Doing great deeds, which we do not know. [6] “For <dn>He</dn> says to the snow, <dq>‘Be on the earth,’</dq> And to the gentle rain and the heavy rain of <dn>His</dn> strength. [7] “<dn>He</dn> seals the hand of every man, That all men might know <dn>His</dn> work. [8] “And the beast goes into its lair, And remains in its dens. [9] “From the Room comes the whirlwind, And cold from the scattering winds. [10] “By the breath of <dn>El</dn> ice is given, And the broad waters become hard. [11] “Also with moisture <dn>He</dn> weighs down the thick cloud; <dn>He</dn> scatters <dn>His</dn> bright cloud, [12] “And they turn around by <dn>His</dn> guidance, To do whatever <dn>He</dn> commands them On the face of the earthly world. [13] “<dn>He</dn> causes it to come, Whether for a rod, or for <dn>His</dn> land, or for kindness. [14] “Listen to this, O Job; Stand still and consider the wonders of <dn>El</dn>. [15] “Do you know when <dn>Eloah</dn> attended to them, And caused the light of <dn>His</dn> cloud to shine? [16] “Do you know the balancings of the clouds, The wonders of the <dn>One</dn> perfect in knowledge? [17] “Why are your garments hot, When the earth is still because of the south wind? [18] “Have you with <dn>Him</dn> spread out the skies, Strong as a hard mirror? [19] “Teach us what we should say to <dn>Him</dn>; We arrange nothing because of darkness. [20] “Should it be told <dn>Him</dn> that I speak? If a man speaks, shall he be swallowed up? [21] “And now, men do not look on the light that is bright in the skies, When the wind has passed and cleared them. [22] “From the golden north it comes; With <dn>Eloah</dn> is awesome majesty. [23] “The <dn>Almighty</dn>, we have not found <dn>Him</dn>; <dn>He</dn> is great in power and right-ruling, And abundant righteousness <dn>He</dn> does not afflict. [24] “Therefore men fear <dn>Him</dn>; <dn>He</dn> sees not all the wise of heart.”
